title: Broken Memories: Detecting and Mitigating Memorization in Diffusion Models with Degraded Generations

problem.claim: Diffusion models may memorize training data, creating privacy and copyright risks.

contributions.claim: Memorization is identified as inducing internal numerical instability that can appear as visually broken artifacts.
The work introduces empirical stability regions based on latent update norms to characterize stable generation behavior.
The work proposes an on-the-fly framework for step-wise detection and adaptive mitigation of memorization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that they are the first to identify memorization-induced internal numerical instability manifested as visually broken artifacts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On Stable Diffusion 1.4, the method achieves detection AUC greater than 0.999.
After mitigation, the reported memorization rate is 0.0%.
The reported mitigation preserves semantic fidelity and image quality without altering prompts or guidance, with approximately 0.01 seconds of overhead per image.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion-model memorization creates privacy and copyright risks.
Memorization is associated with internal numerical instability and broken visual artifacts.
Latent update norms are used to define empirical stability regions.
The stability characterization supports step-wise detection and adaptive mitigation during generation.
Experiments on Stable Diffusion 1.4 report strong detection, zero memorization after mitigation, preserved output properties, and negligible overhead.

source_observation.claim: Memorization may produce detectable numerical instability during generation.

interpretation.claim: Runtime stability signals can serve as indicators of memorization.

application.claim: Monitor latent update norms step by step and trigger adaptive mitigation when stability-region behavior indicates risk.

exception.claim: The abstract reports evaluation on Stable Diffusion 1.4 only.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the training datasets, evaluation protocol, baselines, or mitigation procedure.
Generalization beyond Stable Diffusion 1.4 is not stated.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported results.
